title: The Resonance Lab
summary: Find the resonant frequency, current, power, voltages and Q of a series LCR circuit, and tune it.
subject: physics
learningOutcome: The student can find the resonant frequency of an LC circuit, the current and power at resonance, the voltages across the elements, the quality factor, and the capacitance that tunes a circuit.

levels.title: Natural frequency
levels.adds: Baseline: ω₀ = 1/√(LC) for a capacitor across an inductor (Ex 7.6).
hints: ω₀ = 1/√(LC) with L in henry and C in farad.
The resistance does not enter the natural frequency.

levels.title: At resonance
levels.adds: New idea: at resonance X_L = X_C, so Z = R, the current is maximum and P = V²/R (Ex 7.7, 7.8, Example 7.9).
hints: The two reactances cancel, leaving Z = R.
The power factor is 1, so P = V I.

levels.title: The voltages
levels.adds: More steps: V_L and V_C are equal and opposite, so the LC combination has no drop (Ex 7.8).
hints: Find the resonant ω₀ and the current first.
V_L = I ω₀ L, which can exceed the source voltage.
V_C is equal and opposite in phase, so L and C together drop nothing.

levels.title: Quality factor
levels.adds: New idea: Q = ω₀L/R sets how sharp the resonance is and the voltage magnification (Section 7.6.2).
hints: A small resistance gives a large Q.

levels.title: Tune the circuit
levels.adds: Apply it: choose C for a given frequency, and see how the resonance shifts when L changes (Example 7.10).
hints: If L doubles, f₀ falls by a factor of √2.

misconceptions: The current at resonance is limited by the reactances
The voltage across L cannot exceed the source voltage
Resonance depends on the resistance of the circuit
